lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about luck.
Do you have a lucky number, Sam?
Yes. Seven. I always look for the number seven.
Why?
Because seven is good. Yesterday I won a prize, a present. My ticket was number seven!
Great! Go on. What was the prize?
A cat. A black cat.
A black cat is bad luck, Sam!
Is it? Bad luck? Oh no. I come back home, and the cat is on my bed. Today I wake up, and the cat is on my face.
[laugh] Good luck, Sam!
Touch wood! Bye for now!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is luck and superstitions.
Do you believe in superstitions, Sam?
I'm British, so I believe in rain. And in not walking under a ladder.
In Baku we have the evil eye. A blue bead keeps it away. My grandmother has twelve.
What a coincidence! I have a lucky charm too. It's a sock.
A sock?
I put it on and I won a quiz. Then I wore it again, and I lost. Now I only wear one sock for luck.
Which one?
It depends. I check it first in front of the mirror. Last week I bought a lottery ticket in the sock. The chance was one in a million.
And?
The ticket was in the other sock. And yesterday I ran into my ex. It turned out the sock was inside out.
[laugh] I found out my grandmother also never cuts her nails at night.
Why?
Bad luck. But she cuts them all the time. At noon.
Fingers crossed it works. Knock on wood. See you next time!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is luck, fate and fortune.
Let me tell you a story. Last year, my cousin bought a lottery ticket from an old man on the street.
Beginner's luck?
He had never bought a ticket. He thought the odds were a million to one. And he won a small prize: a television.
A miracle! Against all odds.
But the television didn't work. He ended up taking it back and getting a refund. So the luck was worth ten manats.
[laugh] That's the kind of luck I know. I don't gamble. My ritual is to touch wood whenever I say something good.
Does it work?
Sometimes. Last week I said, "I never have bad luck." I touched the table. The table collapsed.
You jinxed it. Maybe you're not optimistic enough.
Or the table was old. It all worked out in the end: I got a new table.
A question for our listeners: do you believe in luck or in hard work?
Both. I pull off both with a lot of wood. See you next time!
